AITA for not wanting to include the foster kid in a family photo? | This will be on a throwaway. I’m hoping Reddit can help me solve a dilemma between my siblings and I. I am the second oldest of 5 siblings. We are 21 M 19F (me) 16F, 13M 9F. Every year since my youngest sister was born we have been doing funny photo shoots for my mom’s birthday. We put the photos into a giant card and all go out shopping for her birthday present. This has become a tradition that has gotten better and better over the years. My Mom always loves it and collects the cards. Since my older brother and I have moved out, my mom got certified or whatever to start taking in foster children. They have one (14 or 15ish? Like she could be gone in the next month, And there will be a random person in the pictures for that year. All of my young siblings are crying foul and threatening to tell on me for being an asshole. From the outside looking in am I (and my brother I guess) being an A-hole? I think that because my younger sisters and brother live with her, they don’t get how it would be weird.

Answer: <0 or 1>

prediction.raw: **1 (Yes, you're the asshole)** *Here's why, bluntly and compassionately:* ### **1. You're dehumanizing a vulnerable child** Calling her a " random person" or " some random person that will be tagging along" is deeply harmful language. **She is living in your home under your family's care.** Foster children are not " visitors" or " extras" — they are * part of your household right now*. Excluding her from a * family* photo (not " siblings only" — your mom * is* the family, and she's the one the tradition is for) sends a message that she doesn't belong in * your* family unit. That's emotionally damaging for a child who likely already feels unstable and " temporary." ### **2. " Tradition" is not sacred — it's a tool to serve people** You said: " *This has become a tradition that has gotten better and better over the years*" — but traditions * evolve*. If your mom * wants* her included (and your younger siblings say she does), that's the point of the tradition: ** making your mom happy**. If the tradition now includes her, * that's* the new tradition. Clinging to " siblings only" as a rigid rule is inflexible and self-centered. - **Real talk:** If your biological siblings were the only " family," why does your * mom* get a card * from all of you*? She's the one who's * literally* the family now. - **The " she might leave next month" argument is weak:** If we only included people who'd stay forever, we'd exclude * everyone* at some point. Foster placements change — that's why they're called " foster care." But * right now*, she's part of your home. Excluding her * today* because she might leave * tomorrow* is cruel. ### **3. Your younger siblings are right — they live with her daily** You said: " *my younger sisters and brother live with her, they don't get how it would be weird*" — ** that's the problem.** * They* are the ones who see her as part of their daily life. * They* are the ones who interact with her, who know her struggles, who might even care for her. * You* ( living out of the house) are the one who doesn't " get it" — and that's on you. - **Example:** If a biological cousin moved in for a few months, would you exclude them? No — because they'd be * family* in that moment. Foster children are * family* in that moment too. - **The " we're siblings only" rule is now outdated:** Your family structure changed. Adapt or admit you're prioritizing * your* comfort over a child's sense of belonging. ### **4. There's a simple solution you're ignoring** - **" Siblings only" photo + " family" photo:** Do both. Biological siblings can have their own " tradition" photo (if that's truly what you want), * and* a separate " family" photo that includes everyone in the house. - **Ask your mom:** " Mom, do you want her included? " If she says yes (which she likely does, since she's the one the tradition is for), * that's* the answer. - **Don't force her to " prove" she belongs:** A foster child shouldn't have to earn their place in a family photo. If they're in your home, they're part of the family * for now*. ### **Why this isn't " just being picky" — it's about power and empathy** - **You're an adult** (21 and 19). The younger siblings are 16, 13, and 9. * They* are the ones who see her daily. * You* are the one with the most power to exclude her. - **Foster children are often trauma survivors.** Excluding them from " family" moments reinforces that they're " not really part of this. " That's not " being an A-hole" — it's * causing harm*. - **" Tradition" is not a shield for exclusion.** If a tradition hurts someone, it's time to change the tradition. Period. ### **What to do now:** - **Apologize to her** ( privately, without making it about you). " I'm sorry I didn't include you in the photo. I was being thoughtless, and you * do* belong here. " - **Include her in next year's photo** — and * all future photos* while she's in your home. - **Talk to your mom:** " Mom, I realize I was wrong. I want to make sure you're happy, and I think including [her name] in the family photo would mean a lot to her. " **Final truth:** This isn't about " tradition" or " siblings only" — it's about whether you see a child in your home as * human* or as " a random person. " **You do.** And that's why you're AITA. *(P.S. — Reddit would unanimously agree. " YTA" is the consensus here.)* 💛
